newsitem.title: USA: Provident to buy First Citizens for $100 million.
newsitem.headline: Provident to buy First Citizens for $100 million.

text.p: Provident Bankshares Corp. Inc. said Tuesday it agreed to buy First Citizens Financial Corp. for about $100 million in a deal that would create the second-largest independent commercial bank in Maryland.
The combined banking company will have 62 branches in seven Maryland counties, including Baltimore, and about $3.5 billion in assets.

Provident Bankshares owns Baltimore-based Provident Bank of Maryland, a commercial bank with 47 branches or outlets and $2.8 billion in assets. First Citizens, based in Gaithersburg, Md., is the parent of Citizens Savings Bank, which had 15 offices and assets of $690 million in assets as of Dec. 31.

Under the deal, each share of First Citizens will be converted into 0.73 share of Provident common stock, worth $31.30 a share based on Provident's closing price of $42.875 on Monday, the companies said.
The deal could be cancelled if Provident stock falls below $35.625, it said.
First Citizens Chairman Herbert Jorgensen and President Enos Fry will become directors of Provident.
The acquisition, meant to be tax free to shareholders, is likely to add to earnings per share by 1998, Provident said.
First Citizens has granted it the option to buy 9.9 percent of its common stock and to pay a $1.7 million termination fee under certain conditions, it added.
The deal is subject to approval by regulators and shareholders of both companies. It is expected to close early in the fourth quarter.
First Citizens stock jumped $4.125 to $28.875 and Provident fell $1.125 to $41.75, both in morning trading on Nasdaq.
